claims.title: Unassisted quantum random-access information lower bound
claims.scope: uniform independent m-bit records encoded into q qubits before a later uniformly random coordinate query, with average decoding error epsilon
assumptions: the receiver has no preshared system correlated with the sender's encoder
ordinary finite-dimensional quantum data processing and entropy bounds apply
nonclaims: continuous quantum amplitudes do not become parent-universe storage units
the lower bound is not evidence that the actual universe uses a random-access encoding

claims.title: Entanglement-assisted quantum causal-cut factor-two lower bound
claims.scope: uniform m-bit records, receiver-side preshared entanglement independent of the record, q transmitted qubits, and a later coordinate query
assumptions: the receiver's preshared system has zero mutual information with the later record before transmission
the conditional mutual-information increase from a q-qubit transmission is bounded by 2q
nonclaims: the storage and generation cost of preshared entanglement is not included in transmitted-qubit count
entanglement improves the constant but does not remove linear scaling at fixed error

claims.title: Exact dense-coding achievability of the assisted cut bound
claims.scope: exact transmission of an m-bit classical record using preshared Bell pairs and transmitted qubits
assumptions: one Bell pair is available per transmitted qubit
the receiver can perform the corresponding Bell measurements
nonclaims: preshared entanglement is an explicit consumed resource rather than a universally free resource
the theorem concerns internal exact classical payload, not unknown parent communication physics

claims.title: Quantum random-access error converse by inverse binary entropy
claims.scope: fixed m-bit uniform record size and fixed unassisted or entanglement-assisted transmitted-qubit budget
assumptions: the uniform average-error information lower bound applies
binary entropy is inverted on its increasing branch [0,1/2]
nonclaims: the converse does not assert finite-code achievability at equality
zero lower bound means only that this converse no longer excludes exact decoding

claims.title: Weighted-query quantum random-access lower bound
claims.scope: uniform independent source bits with a declared nonuniform later query distribution and weighted average error
assumptions: the coordinatewise-Fano KKT allocation from the classical causal-cut model is used
unassisted quantum information is bounded by q and entanglement-assisted information increase by 2q
nonclaims: the weighted result optimizes the coordinatewise-Fano lower bound rather than proving every finite quantum code optimum
zero-weight coordinates lie outside the declared query support

claims.title: Canonical one-qubit two-to-one and three-to-one random access codes
claims.scope: the declared square and cube Bloch-vector encodings with Pauli-axis query measurements
assumptions: Born probabilities are computed from qubit Bloch vectors
record and query pairs are averaged uniformly
nonclaims: the repository does not prove universal optimality of these finite constructions
the constructions obey but do not saturate the general Fano converse

claims.title: Finite Bloch-geometry random-access certificate
claims.scope: all four two-bit records and eight three-bit records under every canonical Pauli query
assumptions: floating-point checks use the declared analytic tolerance
the code enumerates exactly the finite canonical record and query sets
nonclaims: finite enumeration is not a proof for arbitrary random-access codes
the checker validates the declared construction rather than quantum mechanics experimentally
